theory.intro: Sometimes the length an area formula needs is not given. When the figure contains a right-angled triangle, Pythagoras’ theorem finds that length first, and the area formula follows.
facts: $a^{2}+b^{2}=h^{2}$: **add** the squares to find the hypotenuse, **subtract** them to find a shorter side.
The height of a **trapezium** comes from a right-angled triangle whose base is the horizontal overhang at one end.
Area formulas: triangle $=\frac{bh}{2}$, trapezium $=\frac{h}{2}(a+b)$, kite or rhombus $=\frac{1}{2}xy$, where $x$ and $y$ are the full diagonals.
Keep the Pythagoras result **exact**, such as $\sqrt{65}$, when you substitute it into the area formula.
Round **once**, at the end, and only when the question asks for a rounded answer.
steps: Find the right-angled triangle inside the figure and decide whether the missing length is the hypotenuse or a shorter side.
Use Pythagoras’ theorem to find that length, keeping it exact.
Substitute the length into the matching area formula and round only if the question asks.

workedExamples.solution_text:
The perpendicular height bisects the base, giving a half-base of $10\div2=5\text{ cm}$.

$\begin{aligned}h&=\sqrt{12^{2}-5^{2}}\\&=\sqrt{119}\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}A&=\frac{10\times\sqrt{119}}{2}\\&=5\sqrt{119}\\&\approx54.54\text{ cm}^{2}\end{aligned}$

The horizontal overhang is $23-14=9\text{ cm}$.

$\begin{aligned}h&=\sqrt{15^{2}-9^{2}}\\&=\sqrt{144}\\&=12\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}A&=\frac{12}{2}(14+23)\\&=222\text{ cm}^{2}\end{aligned}$

The overhangs are equal, so each is $(26-14)\div2=6\text{ cm}$.

$\begin{aligned}h&=\sqrt{9^{2}-6^{2}}\\&=\sqrt{45}\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}A&=\frac{\sqrt{45}}{2}(14+26)\\&=20\sqrt{45}\\&\approx134.2\text{ cm}^{2}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}a&=\sqrt{10^{2}-6^{2}}\\&=8\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}b&=\sqrt{15^{2}-6^{2}}\\&=\sqrt{189}\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$

The full horizontal diagonal is $2\times6=12\text{ cm}$. The full vertical diagonal is $(8+\sqrt{189})\text{ cm}$.

$\begin{aligned}A&=\frac{12(8+\sqrt{189})}{2}\\&=48+6\sqrt{189}\text{ cm}^{2}\end{aligned}$

The diagonals bisect each other at right angles. Half the known diagonal is $16\div2=8\text{ cm}$.

$\begin{aligned}m&=\sqrt{17^{2}-8^{2}}\\&=\sqrt{225}\\&=15\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$

The other full diagonal is $2\times15=30\text{ cm}$.

$\begin{aligned}A&=\frac{16\times30}{2}\\&=240\text{ cm}^{2}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}x^{2}+x^{2}&=16^{2}\\2x^{2}&=256\\x^{2}&=128\end{aligned}$

The area is $x^{2}$, so there is no need to find $x$.

$A=128\text{ cm}^{2}$

The perpendicular height bisects the base, so each half is $6\text{ cm}$.

$\begin{aligned}h&=\sqrt{12^{2}-6^{2}}\\&=\sqrt{108}\\&=6\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}A&=\frac{12\times6\sqrt{3}}{2}\\&=36\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^{2}\end{aligned}$
